title: Fewer Clicks, More Purchases
eligible_reason: Customers adopt one-click buying in different months. Table 1 (main text, three columns) estimates plm(y ~ factor(month) + postentry, model='within', index='customer') on the full panel: customer FE, month FE, binary postentry that switches on at the customer's adoption month, no controls, never-adopters as comparison. Shipped random sample: 214 adopters in 9 adoption cohorts (months 13-21) and 3,790 never-adopters, balanced 35-month panel, no switch-offs, no duplicate customer-months.
design_notes: R plm/lm. The authors' preferred analysis is rolling-entry matching (rollmatch) with matched-pair comparisons (Tables 3, 6, 7) and causal forests (Tables 4-5); Table 1 is the pre-matching staggered TWFE panel regression. Table A3 re-runs TWFE on matched data with treatment*postentry; Table A4 checks pre-period trends on matched data.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: In the shipped sample adoption months are 13-21 (27, 16, 13, 26, 26, 16, 25, 31, 34 customers); the full panel may contain more cohorts.

data_files_note: ReadMe: data.long.sample.rds is a random sample of the paper's panel (214 treated and 3,790 control customers, 35 months, 140,140 rows; customer ids altered); results will differ from the paper (about 20% of the paper's matched pairs).
data_provenance_note: Random subsample of original retailer data; no noise or synthetic values mentioned. Counts as original data with the random_subsample flag (5b).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Eligible on Table 1 only; the published coefficients come from the full panel, so the TWFE replication on the shipped sample will be approximate (random-subsample flag).
preferred_note: Authors prefer the matched-pair estimates (Table 3); Table 1 is the before-matching panel estimate.
